subject: English
passage: In 2014, a cache of roughly 3,500-year-old ostrich eggshell fragments bearing clusters of small incised marks was recovered from a Bronze Age caravan waystation in the southern Arabian Peninsula. Although most scholars hold that formal record-keeping in the region emerged only with later Sabaean inscriptions, archaeologist Asha Banerjee contends that these fragments may indicate that earlier traders kept tallies of goods. The incised marks are irregularly grouped but consistently shallow, and residue analysis indicates that they were produced with a single copper blade; according to Banerjee, this implies that the marks were inscribed in one sitting by a single trader to record quantities of a traded commodity.
prompt: Which finding, if true, would most directly weaken the underlined claim?

choices.A: Irregularly grouped incisions are a recurring feature in the earliest known record-keeping systems developed by Sabaean scribes.
choices.B: More than a dozen irregularly grouped incisions produced with a different copper blade appear on another eggshell fragment recovered at a Bronze Age site in the Arabian Peninsula.
choices.C: It would have required careful effort to produce consistently shallow incisions on eggshell using the copper blades typically available to Bronze Age traders.
choices.D: Ornamental objects found at another Bronze Age waystation in the southern Arabian Peninsula predominantly display patterns of irregularly grouped incised marks.

explanation: Choice D is the best answer. Banerjee bases her claim on the fact that the eggshell fragments feature irregularly grouped incised marks produced with a single blade. But if ornamental objects at another Bronze Age waystation in the same region predominantly display patterns of irregularly grouped incised marks, it would suggest that the fragments are more likely decorative than records of traded quantities — undermining the inference that the marks were made to tally goods.
